result.decision_rationale:
The production cast release no longer advances the creator, and witness reconciliation now uses probe-wide attribution. Both focused gates and the short native session passed. Two required observations remain inconclusive in the domain fixture.

Continuation for Claude

Complete the two observations in the existing focused test. Connect the simulated creator to the exercised cast boundary so that a tick there would visibly register the queued foreign unit. In the two-witness case, distinguish a request made during final reconciliation from the registered control’s later fixture teardown. Keep the shared production release and finalizer in both tests. Run `sprint7-visual` and `loader-compat-probe` through the controller on the corrected commit. A domain-test-only correction can reuse session `20261126T033419Z` under OWNER AMENDMENT 2 when the harness and session bytes match. C3 retains combined product qualification.

required_gaps: R3-F1 needs a participating simulated creator whose advancement is observable through the exercised cast boundary.
R4-F1 needs an observation that identifies when the independently registered foreign control receives its sole request during final release.
source_inspection_only: The held cast callback reads the retained summon, excludes the registered reference and uses the per-reference request guard. The remaining EntityCreator.Tick call is in ordinary forward cast progression.

The shared finalizer places all witness reconciliations before ReleaseRemaining. That ordering explains the registered control’s request in the current source. The fixture’s counters do not independently establish its origin.

findings.actual: The fixture adds ForeignQueued to Creation.Queued, then supplies plain field readers to OwnedCastRelease.Hold. CreationQueue.Tick has no caller and is never bound to a simulated engine operation. Its zero count and the foreign unit’s pending flag therefore cannot detect a tick added to the native cast callback.
findings.blocking_rationale: OWNER AMENDMENT 2 explicitly requires a participating controlled creation queue. The source correction and native real-spawn result establish other parts of R3-F1, but the required regression cannot detect the foreign registration it claims to check.
findings.expected: Advancing the creator at the exercised boundary would register the exact queued foreign unit. Synchronous abandonment leaves it pending and unrequested.
findings.requested_correction: Connect the fixture’s simulated creator to the cast boundary used by the shared held release. For example, a domain control can model the former tick immediately before the retained-summon read and demonstrate that the same foreign unit registers.
findings.requested_evidence: Show that the control detects an advance, then that the actual ProbeSlot.Abandon path leaves the foreign unit queued in the no-summon, conclusively destroyed and pending-summon cases. Retain the original timeout, independent releases and named pending residual.
findings.title: The abandonment test cannot observe a creator tick
findings.trigger: ProbeSlot abandons a held cast while a foreign unit is queued for creation.

findings.actual: SharedWitnessProbe sets Reconciling around early and held releases, then clears it before LateUnitFinalRelease.Release. Both final witness reconciliation and ReleaseRemaining run with the flag false. A premature final-witness request would consume the one-request guard and still satisfy both asserted counts for a registered foreign control.
findings.blocking_rationale: OWNER AMENDMENT 2 requires the focused evidence to distinguish preservation during witness reconciliation from authorized fixture teardown. The unregistered-control variants establish survival throughout, but the registered variant cannot identify which final operation removed it.
findings.expected: The registered foreign control has zero requests through the last witness reconciliation and receives its single request during fixture teardown.
findings.requested_correction: Make the request’s origin observable in the existing fixture. One test-only option is to register a teardown-only unit ahead of the foreign control and record destruction order. A premature witness request for the foreign unit would then precede that unit’s teardown.
findings.requested_evidence: Through the shared finalizer, distinguish the registered control’s teardown request from a final witness request in both witness orders. Keep the genuine unknown, original unsubscribe failure and next-Begin refusal assertions.
findings.title: The registered foreign control’s final request has no observable origin
findings.trigger: The two-witness fixture registers the foreign control for teardown and final reconciliation runs after the held callbacks.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: The production correction is present. CastOwned installs the shared exact-reference release, and the focused case exercises its one-request and pending-settlement behavior through ProbeSlot.Abandon. The disposition remains incomplete because the simulated creator is disconnected from that boundary. OWNER AMENDMENT 2 specifically requires this observation.

Every production witness registers its observation in the same probe-local attribution view. Early, held and final reconciliation consult that view by reference before recording uncertainty. The executed two-witness cases cover both orders, retain the genuine unknown and unsubscribe error, request the matched summon once and refuse the next Begin. R4-F1 concerns the separate timing evidence for registered-control destruction.
The settlement reader requires a JArray. The passing focused case explicitly accepts an empty array and rejects both an absent field and a scalar.

summary.delivered_behavior: Cast cleanup requests the exact retained summon once. Witness callers reconcile positive matches and explicit controls across the probe, preserve genuine uncertainty, and return a shared final settlement snapshot to ProbeSlot.
